reason: Our unit and end-to-end tests in CI already catch what the agent breaks in the PRs I merge, so I don't have a painful gap this would fill. Recording sessions and then reviewing a list of business rules an AI guessed sounds like a second test suite I'd have to babysit.
objection: Field-by-field diffs between old and new versions will be full of noise from timestamps, IDs and intentional changes, and I'd spend more time triaging false alarms than I spend writing a test today. I also don't trust an AI-explored sandbox to cover the edge cases that actually bite us.
would_change_my_mind: An agent PR that passes all our tests and still breaks something in production, plus proof that Parity would have caught it with near-zero false positives on a repo like ours.
